problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨{e}^{t},\,-t{e}^{t},\,2t⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=0\,\text{s}.$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating Components of Acceleration at a Particular Moment
examples.problem: The position $\mathbf r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)= \langle e^{2t}, \, e^{-t} , \, 1 \rangle,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t = 0\,\textrm s.$
examples.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t = 0,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{2t},\,-{e}^{-t},\,0⟩, \\ v(0) & =⟨2{e}^{2(0)},\,-{e}^{-0},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t = 0{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{e}^{2t},\,{e}^{-t},\,0,⟩ \\ a(0) & =⟨4{e}^{2(0)},\,{e}^{-0},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\mathbf v(0) \cdot \mathbf a(0)$ and $||\mathbf v(0)||\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0)\cdot a(0) & =⟨2,\,-1,\,0⟩\cdot ⟨4,\,1,\,0⟩ \\  & =7, \\ ||v(0)|| & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=0,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(0)\cdot a(0)}{||v(0)||} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $\dfrac{7\sqrt{5}}{5} \, \textrm{ms}^{-2}.$

feedback.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},\,-6,\,-{t}^{3}⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-6),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,0,\,-3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨2t,\,0,\,-3{t}^{2}⟩\times ⟨2,\,0,\,-6t⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & 0 & -3{t}^{2} \\ 2 & 0 & -6t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}0 & -3{t}^{2} \\ 0 & -6t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2t & -3{t}^{2} \\ 2 & -6t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 0 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,-(-12{t}^{2}+6{t}^{2}),0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,6{t}^{2},0⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(2t)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(-3{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}(9{t}^{2}+4)} \\  & =t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(6{t}^{2})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =6{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{6{t}^{2}}{t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}} \\  & =\frac{6t}{\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}}.\end{aligned}
$$
